title: Include offline observability artifacts in air-gapped bundle + update manifest
author: Connor O'Brien
description: Context: Several on-prem / air-gapped Private installs reported Grafana coming up without any Redwood dashboards after install/upgrade because the offline bundle did not include the minimum-pack dashboard JSONs and Prometheus rules (SUP-49210, Slack thread: airgap-bundle-missing-grafana-dashboards). This PR updates the air-gap bundle build so the observability artifacts are shipped as first-class, versioned bundle contents. What changed: (1) add observability artifacts to the airgap bundle payload: Grafana dashboard bundle (runtime + control plane), Prometheus alerting/recording rules, and default log collector configs; (2) update the bundle manifest schema usage to explicitly list these artifacts under the 'artifacts' section with stable filenames and SHA256s; (3) wire extraction/install into post-unpack steps so upgrades can safely rehydrate dashboards/rules without requiring outbound fetches; (4) add a lightweight validation step in the bundle build pipeline to fail if any referenced observability artifact path is missing. Notes/constraints: No customer data is embedded; artifacts are static JSON/YAML shipped with the installer. This does not enable/disable observability components by default; it only ensures the offline bundle contains the required files when customers enable the minimum pack via Helm values. Backward compatibility: Existing bundle consumers continue to work; new manifest entries are additive. Follow-ups: noise tuning and runbook links live in the observability-pack rules PRs; this PR only handles packaging and offline delivery.
commits: airgap: include grafana dashboards and prometheus rules in bundle payload
bundle-manifest: add artifact entries + sha256 generation for observability files
installer: extract observability artifacts to shared dir for helm wiring
ci: add bundle build assertion for missing observability paths
docs: update onprem airgap bundle README with new artifacts list
conversation: Fatima Noor (review): Can we confirm the bundle build does not attempt to fetch dashboards from the internet at build time? Air-gapped customers won’t have that option and our internal build sometimes runs in restricted networks too.

Connor O'Brien (author): Yep — all files are sourced from the repo under packaging/airgap/artifacts/observability. The build script only copies local files + computes sha256. I added a CI assertion to fail if any path is missing so we don’t silently produce an incomplete bundle.

Chloe Martin (review): Dashboard filenames: please keep them stable and versioned; Grafana provisioning can be sensitive if we rename on upgrades. Suggest prefixing with private-min-pack-v1-*.json and keeping a top-level index file optional.

Connor O'Brien (author): Done. Renamed to private-min-pack-v1-runtime.json, private-min-pack-v1-control-plane.json, and private-min-pack-v1-infra.json. Also updated the manifest entries so the artifact IDs are stable even if we add more dashboards later.

Kevin Osei (review - security): Log configs: please double-check we’re not shipping example configs that encourage logging request payloads by default. Also ensure the manifest doesn’t include anything that looks like a secret (tokens, endpoints).

Connor O'Brien (author): Good catch. The shipped collector config is the baseline redaction-safe config (no body logging; includes request_id and hashed tenant_id only). No endpoints/tokens in the repo artifacts — sinks are documented as placeholders only. Updated docs to explicitly call out that secrets must be provided via Kubernetes Secrets.
Rafael Mendes (review - SRE): Can we add a simple post-unpack check that surfaces a clear error if dashboards are missing? This would have saved us time in SUP-49210.

Connor O'Brien (author): Added installer/post_install/validate_bundle_contents.sh and wired it into the airgap smoke test. It fails fast with a list of missing artifact paths and points to the on-prem runbook section.

Diego Santos (review): Upgrade behavior: we should avoid overwriting customer-modified dashboards if they’ve edited them in-cluster. Are we writing into a separate directory that Helm picks up, vs pushing directly into Grafana via API?

Connor O'Brien (author): We only extract into the installer’s shared artifacts directory (used by Helm chart provisioning). We’re not pushing to Grafana APIs. Customer customization in-cluster remains their responsibility; our extracted bundle is treated as immutable inputs to provisioning.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main; included in the next private-installer release bundle. No backport requested yet, but marked as release-blocker for upcoming on-prem validation.
release_notes: Air-gapped bundle now includes the Private observability minimum pack artifacts (Grafana dashboards, Prometheus rules, and default log collector configs).
Bundle manifest lists observability artifacts with SHA256 checksums for integrity verification.
Airgap bundle build fails fast if required observability artifacts are missing.
